name: Transmon memory with two storage resonators
question: What fraction of a single photon sent into the readout resonator comes back out in the expected temporal mode after the transmon has stored it in one storage resonator, moved it to a second one and released it, and where are the lost photons absorbed?
assumptions: Every element in the frame rotating at its own frequency; the couplings are parametric (tunable couplers or sideband drives) and resonant while they are on, so each acts as an exchange g (a^dagger b + h.c.); hbar = 1; rates and times in units of the readout line rate kappa.

Each swap is a pi/2 pulse of the exchange, g t = pi/2, which moves one excitation completely between two elements; the dispersive shifts between transmon and resonators act only on states with two excitations and are left out.
The transmon keeps three levels with anharmonicity alpha; in the one-photon sector the third level is not reached, and its population is recorded as a check.

The input photon rises exponentially at the readout line rate, the temporal mode that an empty resonator absorbs completely; the output mode is the decaying exponential that the readout resonator emits once the photon is back in it.

Loss rates of the order of transmon and resonator lifetimes in circuit QED (T1 of a few hundred and storage lifetimes of about a thousand inverse line rates); they are illustrative, not fitted to a device.

provenance.reference: catch and release of itinerant photons in circuit QED: J. Wenner et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 112, 210501 (2014); P. Kurpiers et al., Nature 558, 264 (2018); multimode storage behind a transmon: R. K. Naik et al., Nat. Commun. 8, 1904 (2017); input and output pulses: A. H. Kiilerich and K. Moelmer, Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 123604 (2019)
